summary: Singapore's Immigration & Checkpoints Authority says the period of stay is determined by the Visit Pass issued as an e-Pass at the checkpoint on entry, not by any visa. Its list of travel documents that need a visa includes India, Russia and Pakistan among others; Singapore's embassy in Beijing says holders of ordinary Chinese passports are exempt from visas for a stay of up to 30 days from 9 February 2024. ICA says all travellers must submit the free SG Arrival Card within three days, including the day of arrival, before arriving.

conditionalWaivers.text: ICA says nationals of India and holders of a PRC Travel Document, a Hong Kong SAR Document of Identity or a Macau SAR Travel Permit (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, public affairs and service PRC passports are excluded) may be eligible for the 96-hour Visa-Free Transit Facility when in transit to or from a third country, with a valid onward air, ferry or cruise ticket departing within 96 hours and a valid visa or long-term pass (valid at least one month from entry) for Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the United Kingdom or the United States. Nationals of the CIS states (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan), Georgia, Turkmenistan and Ukraine need a valid onward air ticket departing within 96 hours and must depart by air. Extension of stay under the facility is strictly not allowed.

source.name: ICA — Visa-Free Transit Facility

fee.notes: ICA says a S$30 non-refundable processing fee is payable online using a Visa or MasterCard credit or debit card, and that applications can be submitted online through a strategic partner or a local contact in Singapore, or at a Singapore Overseas Mission or through its authorised visa agent.

vaccinations.text: ICA says all travellers who have been in a country with risk of yellow fever transmission in the six days before arriving in Singapore must produce a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate on arrival, including those who spent more than 12 hours in airport transit in such a country.

declarations.name: SG Arrival Card (SGAC)
declarations.text: ICA says all travellers must submit the SG Arrival Card with electronic health declaration within three days, including the day of arrival, before arriving, except those transiting without seeking immigration clearance and residents entering through Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints. Submission is free, via the SGAC e-Service or the MyICA app; travellers who fail to submit it may be denied entry.

source.name: ICA — SG Arrival Card (SGAC) with Electronic Health Declaration

currencyLimits.text: ICA says that if you enter or leave Singapore carrying physical currency and bearer negotiable instruments with a total value exceeding S$20,000 (or its equivalent in a foreign currency), you are required by law to make a declaration (Form NP 727) to the Singapore Police Force.

source.name: ICA — Taking cash in and out of Singapore

notes: The UK government says vapes and e-cigarettes are banned in Singapore: it is illegal to bring them into the country, including for personal use, and those found in possession of them will have them confiscated and could be fined.

The UK government lists among items illegal to bring into Singapore vaporisers and e-cigarettes, tobacco products that are chewed or injected, chewing gum to sell, weapons and ammunition, and replica guns.
Australia's Smartraveller says penalties for the use and possession of drugs include caning and the mandatory death sentence for some trafficking offences.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says violent crime and theft are rare in Singapore. Australia's Smartraveller says Singapore has strict laws and penalties for acts that are legal or minor offences in Australia, including littering and jaywalking.

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit Singapore. Canada's travel advice says the rainy (or monsoon) season extends from December to March in the northeast and June to September in the southeast.

idp.text: Singapore is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). The Singapore Police Force says a foreigner residing in Singapore for less than 12 months who holds a valid foreign driving licence does not need to convert it (with listed exceptions), and must have the foreign driving licence and an International Driving Permit issued by an authorised body from their country of origin, or an official English translation of the foreign licence if an IDP is not available. It says foreigners from an ASEAN member state do not need an IDP.

tips.text: ICA says submitting the SG Arrival Card is free of charge and that commercial entities offering to submit it for a fee are not affiliated with ICA. Submit it via the SGAC e-Service or the MyICA app within three days, including the day of arrival, before you arrive.

The UK government says vapes and e-cigarettes are banned in Singapore: it is illegal to bring them into the country, including for personal use, and those found in possession of them will have them confiscated and could be fined.

Australia's Smartraveller says Singapore has strict laws and penalties for acts that are legal or minor offences in Australia, including smoking in public, spitting, importing or chewing gum, chewing tobacco, littering and jaywalking, and that penalties for drug offences include caning and the mandatory death sentence for some trafficking offences.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Singapore?
faq.answer: No visa is required: the US State Department gives the tourist visa requirement as not required for stays under 90 days. Singapore's ICA says the period of stay is set by the Visit Pass issued as an e-Pass at the checkpoint on entry, and that all travellers must submit the free SG Arrival Card within three days, including the day of arrival, before arriving.

faq.question: What is the SG Arrival Card and who needs it?
faq.answer: ICA says the SG Arrival Card is the electronic version of the paper disembarkation/embarkation card, submitted with an electronic health declaration. All travellers must submit it within three days, including the day of arrival, before arriving, except those transiting without seeking immigration clearance and residents entering through Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints. Submission is free, via the SGAC e-Service or the MyICA app, and the SG Arrival Card is not a visa.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens visit Singapore without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Singapore's embassy in Beijing says that from 9 February 2024 holders of ordinary passports issued by the People's Republic of China are exempt from visa requirements for a stay of up to 30 days. ICA says all travellers must also submit the SG Arrival Card before arriving.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Singapore?
faq.answer: Yes. ICA says you need a visa to enter Singapore with an Indian travel document (holders of diplomatic, official and service passports excepted). The application can be submitted online through a strategic partner or a local contact in Singapore, or at a Singapore Overseas Mission or through its authorised visa agent; a S$30 non-refundable processing fee applies, and applications are processed within three working days. The SG Arrival Card must also be submitted before arrival.

faq.question: Can I bring cigarettes or a vape into Singapore?
faq.answer: Vapes: no — the UK government says vapes and e-cigarettes are banned in Singapore and illegal to bring in, including for personal use. Cigarettes: no official source we could read sets out the duty rules; ICA says to declare all dutiable goods at the Red Channel.

countryFacts.driving.text: There is no need for conversion of licence if you are a foreigner residing in Singapore for less than 12 months holding a valid foreign driving licence except the following,
If you are a foreigner residing in Singapore for less than 12 months, you must:
Possess a foreign driving licence and *International Driving Permit (IDP) issued by an authorised body from your country of origin; or
Possess an official translation of your foreign driving licence in ^English if an IDP is not available.
However, if you are a foreigner from an ASEAN member state, you do not need an IDP. Please ensure you have a valid foreign driving licence.

If you are in transit to or from any third country via Singapore, you may be eligible for the 96-hour VFTF if you meet these requirements: You may enter Singapore by any mode of transport but depart only via air or sea. You must have a valid onward air/ferry/cruise ticket departing Singapore within 96 hours; and You must have a valid visa[3] or long-term pass (with a validity of at least one month from the date of entry into Singapore under the VFTF) issued by and/or good for entry into any of the following countries: - Australia - Canada - Germany - Japan - New Zealand - Switzerland - United Kingdom - United States of America
[1] CIS refers to: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Russia, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan.

Nationals of the CIS[1], Georgia, Turkmenistan and Ukraine If you are in transit to or from any third country, you may be eligible for the 96-hour VFTF if you have a valid onward air ticket departing within 96 hours. You may enter Singapore by any mode of transport but must depart Singapore by air.
Extension of stay for transit travellers under VFTF is strictly not allowed.
